extracted.intended_audience: humor researchers, theorists, and joke writers (scholar-practitioners interested in incongruity theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing whether an instance of incongruity will produce humor by checking additional cognitive, contextual, affective, and target-selection conditions; also guidance for constructing jokes that go beyond mere incongruity. Useful for scholars analyzing humorous cases and practitioners designing jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of incongruity (necessary condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity is a necessary but not sufficient condition for humor: an incongruity must be present for comedic potential, but by itself it does not guarantee amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cundall documents many phenomena that instantiate incongruity yet do not produce humor (examples: surprise, confusion, awe, horror, mystery, tragedy). Use the presence of incongruity as a starting point, but do not assume humor will follow without additional conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptual readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience must be in a perceptual stance prepared to play with the incongruity, not to take it seriously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the audience is primed to 'play' (warm-up matters). If the audience is oriented to seriousness, the same incongruity may elicit shock, confusion, or offense rather than amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play frame / safe context
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be contextual cues (genre, social setting, speaker tone) that signal 'this is for amusement,' not 'this is real.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit play-frame cues such as comedic genre markers, ironic tone, or social signals that create a safe frame. The medium and stage signals (e.g., comedy club vs. news broadcast) matter; absent a play frame, incongruity will often be interpreted non-comically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizable resolution path
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a discoverable way to make sense of the incongruity — not necessarily a clean resolution, but enough cognitive traction that the audience can engage with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the audience can find a resolution or reinterpretation that accounts for the incongruity. If no resolution path is perceptible, the result may be confusion or puzzlement rather than laughter. Clarity and solvability of the incongruity are important in joke design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affective tolerability (benignness threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the incongruity, even when negative or transgressive, must be tolerable to the audience; beyond a threshold the incongruity becomes painful rather than funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibrate content to audience sensitivities. This condition overlaps with 'benign violation' — the incongruity must be construed as a benign violation for humor to arise. If the affective impact crosses the audience's tolerance threshold, the response will be offense, disgust, or distress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate target / object selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The incongruity must concern an object whose disturbance is acceptable; sacred objects, beloved persons, or deep traumas may resist comic framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the target of the incongruity is within the comic-acceptable range for the audience. Sensitive or protected targets can block a humorous reading even when other conditions obtain; target-selection is a distinct constraint on comedic viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical verification procedure (six-step checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommended procedure for assessing candidate humor instances: 1) Identify the incongruity precisely. 2) Verify whether the audience has perceptual readiness. 3) Verify whether play-frame cues are present. 4) Verify whether resolution is achievable. 5) Verify whether the content is affectively tolerable. 6) Verify whether the object is in the comic-acceptable range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this stepwise diagnostic: if any condition fails, the same incongruity will likely produce a different response (surprise, confusion, awe, horror, offense). This is both an evaluative rubric and a practical checklist for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications for joke construction (practical checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designers must ensure not just incongruity but also that: the audience is primed to play; stage/medium signals 'this is comedy'; the incongruity is solvable; the content is within audience tolerance; and targets are acceptably disposable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete design guidance: warm up and prime audiences; choose venues and genres that supply play-frame cues; craft incongruities with discoverable resolutions; calibrate transgression and negativity to audience norms; avoid targets likely to be protected or sacralized by this audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic questions for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of targeted questions to apply to a candidate humorous instance: What is the precise incongruity? Is the audience in a play-prepared state? Are there explicit play-frame cues? Is there a resolution path the audience can find? Does the content stay within the audience's affective tolerance? Are the targets in the comically-acceptable range for this audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these questions as a rapid assessment tool during analysis or rehearsal. They operationalize the six verification steps and help identify which condition(s) are failing when an incongruity does not produce humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with benign violation theory (conceptual mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cundall's additional conditions converge with McGraw & Warren's benign violation theory: the extra constraints can be summarized as the 'benignness' of the violation, but decomposed into perceptual, contextual, cognitive, affective, and target-selection components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use benign-violation as an umbrella concept while relying on Cundall's finer-grained checklist to diagnose specific failures (e.g., perceptual readiness vs. affective tolerance). This mapping helps integrate Cundall's framework with existing empirical theories.
